The new text keeps the Hook and validation-predicate halves verbatim and says an unlowerable `SharingRule` `condition` fails the build and, at runtime, the rule is skipped and grants nothing (one WARN). Spot reads on `main`: `packages/lint/src/validate-sharing-rule-enforceability.ts:18-28` (error at build; SKIPPED at runtime), `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/declared-sharing-rules.ts:45-48` (skipped, never served as match-all) and `:336-348`, `:372-373` (`warnOnce` then `continue`). ## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f768c9213ef3fa8977c43c61536d4f07f24e4e3d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md + none
Security-touching: yes

PR #36562 · card #36516 · net diff against `main` (merge-base d463c46f): 2 files, `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` (+4 −6) and `.changeset/36516-formula-skill-sharing-rule-skip.md` (+12). No implementing file is in the diff; the code the sentence describes was read on `origin/main` (3b589215), where none of `skills/objectstack-formula/**`, `packages/lint/src/validate-sharing-rule-enforceability.ts` or `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/**` has moved since the merge-base.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: unchanged. No schema, validator, lint rule, runtime or CLI file is in the diff; nothing a stack author writes is newly accepted or refused. Right.
- Public surface: the published text of one skill (`@objectstack/skills`, `objectstack-formula/SKILL.md`). One teaching sentence changes meaning (the `SharingRule` half of the fail-closed warning), two restatements are removed. Frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `version`) is untouched, so trigger behaviour does not change. Right.
- Eval set: unchanged. Case 14 at this head already expects "do not lower there, and the rule would grant nothing"; case 3 already expects the `previous`-on-insert fault and the `previous != null &&` guard. The corrected sentence now agrees with case 14 where the old one contradicted it. Right.
- Token ratchet: `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` is not in the diff; the formula row reads 6008 at this head. Ceiling not raised. Right.
- Check-runs on this head: 45 total, 29 success, 16 skipped (UI, docs, dogfood-matrix, temporal, queue and opt-in jobs a skills-only diff does not select), 0 failed, 0 pending. `Check Changeset`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Core`, `Test Core` all success. These are the gate verdicts; nothing was re-run.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/36516-formula-skill-sharing-rule-skip.md`: `'@objectstack/skills': patch`. The package exists under that name (`packages/skills/package.json`). A wording correction with no accept-set or API change is a patch. Matches.
- Clause-②: no — on the PR body and in the changeset, and correct: nothing that validated before is refused after, and nothing is removed from a published schema or API. `Metadata-protocol: none` is likewise correct.
- The changeset body agrees with the diff sentence by sentence (the corrected warning, the two cuts and where each still lives). One reading note, not a ④ finding because changesets are outside ④: "A sharing rule's condition is never evaluated on a write" is true of the CEL text (it is lowered once to a filter and never interpreted), while the lowered criteria query does run at boot and on later writes to keep grants current. The following clause ("it is compiled to a query filter") makes the intended meaning clear.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation "4 build-dependent gate families NOT MEASURED locally" (dts-closure, dual-build-cjs-loads, lean-entry-closure, sourcemap-no-sources-content): answered by the head's check-runs, all green; a text-only diff cannot move them.
- Dev deviation "no eval case added": answered. Case 14 exists at this head and pins the skip; a second case would restate it.
- Dev deviations on commit trailers and the PR body's first line: process shape, outside the contract face; left to the lane seat's ACCEPT.
- `open_questions`: empty. `out_of_scope_findings`: empty. Nothing to escalate.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no code in the diff, so no new id materialisation or in-app join. The behaviour the sentence teaches is itself the push-down path (CEL lowered to a filter by the one canonical compiler); the text does not suggest an in-app alternative.
- Security: the changed hunk teaches sharing-rule (record access) failure behaviour, so `Security-touching` is `yes` and is meant; the adopting seat adds the `security` label.

### ④ Design judgment

`skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` — the corrected sentence, read word by word against `main`:

> an unevaluable `Hook` `condition` or validation predicate **aborts the write** (§5); a `SharingRule` `condition` that does not lower to a filter fails the build, and at runtime the rule is skipped and grants nothing (one WARN).

- "`Hook` `condition` or validation predicate aborts the write (§5)": the words of the old sentence minus `SharingRule`; §5's "An unevaluable condition ABORTS the operation" paragraph still carries it. Unchanged teaching.
- "does not lower to a filter fails the build": `validateSharingRuleEnforceability` calls `compileCelToFilter(input, { variables: {} })` and pushes `severity: 'error'` for both refusal classes it owns (`sharing-rule-unlowerable-condition`, `sharing-rule-runtime-variable-condition`); the third, `parse-error`, is left to `validateStackExpressions`, which is also `tier: 'gating'`, `commands: ALL`. The rule is registered `tier: 'gating'`, `commands: ALL` in `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts`, and `packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts` runs `runAuthoringRules('build', …)`, splits by severity and exits 1 on any error ("Author-time rules failed"). `os validate` and `os lint` run the same table. True. Tried to break it: every reason the compiler can refuse for maps to a gating error, so there is no unlowerable condition that builds green through the CLI.
- "at runtime the rule is skipped": `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/declared-sharing-rules.ts` — `celToFilterOutcome` makes the same compiler call with the same options; `translateDeclaredSharingRule` returns `{ skip: { kind: 'condition', … } }` on a null filter; `list()` calls `warnOnce` and `continue`s, so the rule never enters the served set; `lookup()` answers `not-found` for it. True. The runtime half is not dead text behind the build gate: the lint entry is `surfaces: CLI_ONLY` (the Studio / REST / MCP publish door does not run it yet) and a stale pre-built package can still register such a rule, so an author can meet the skip.
- "and grants nothing": the skipped rule is never translated to criteria, so no `sys_record_share` row is written from it; the module header and the lint header both state it is never served as a permissive match-all (ADR-0049). Fail-closed: the recipient under-sees. This is what makes it sit correctly under "the opposite holds" of the fault-OPEN `visibleWhen` the paragraph opens with. True.
- "(one WARN)": `warnOnce` keys on rule name and cause and logs once per process through `opts.logger?.warn`, with the compiler's `reason` and `detail` in the meta. True as shorthand.
- Against the card: the card asks for exactly this — only the `SharingRule` half changes, build refuses, runtime grants nothing. Held. Against eval case 14: the skill body no longer contradicts the case's expected output.

Payment hunks:

- Cut 1, the note under the translation table (`previous.x` fails the write on an insert unless guarded by `previous != null &&`): every element still stands in the file at this head. §5's `previous` table, Insert row: "`previous != null && …` skips one; a column read off it (`previous.x`) has no value and faults". §5's ABORTS paragraph: a column read off `previous` on an insert "fails the write". The cheat-sheet's "Previous record" row points to §5. Eval case 3 pins the behaviour. No teaching is lost.
- Cut 2, "Two more dialects ride the same envelope.": Core contract still opens with "Every expression in metadata is the same envelope" and its table lists `cron` and `template` as registered dialects. The remaining sentence, "Neither dialect is CEL; both take a bare string (auto-wrapped) or their helper", reads correctly under the heading "Cron and template surfaces", which supplies the referent. No teaching is lost.

N1 (nit) — Cut 1 removes the only reminder that sat at the point of use, directly under the `OLD.x` and `ISCHANGED(x)` rows that emit `previous.x`. The table itself now carries no pointer to §5. The skill is loaded whole and §5, the cheat-sheet row and eval case 3 still teach it, so correctness and the contract are unaffected. Accepted deviation; if headroom returns, a ` — §5` suffix on the `ISCHANGED(x)` row would restore the pointer for a few bytes.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
